prompt: Build a tiny {{placeholder}} template engine with chainable set calls, verbatim pass-through for unknown keys, and a missingKeys report. Complete the three methods, then run the tests.
explanation: Rendering is a scan, not a series of replace calls: indexOf("{{", i) finds the next placeholder and indexOf("}}", open + 2) finds its end, so the text between i and open is copied literally and the slice between the braces is trimmed into a key. Checking containsKey rather than get lets an unset key be echoed verbatim instead of printing null, and a missing "}}" simply copies the rest of the template. Returning this from set is the builder trick that makes calls chain.
hints: Walk the template with an index: find the next "{{", copy everything before it, then find the matching "}}".
template.substring(open + 2, close).trim() is the key -- trim() is what makes {{ name }} and {{name}} the same.
Use values.containsKey(key) to decide between appending the stored value and appending the raw placeholder text template.substring(open, close + 2). Return this from set so calls can be chained.
